card.name: Thabal Chongba
card.tagline: Manipuri Meitei moonlight circle dance during Yaoshang
card.profile: Thabal Chongba (Meitei: thabal = moonlight, chongba = dance) is a Manipuri folk dance in which young men and women join hands in concentric circles and dance under the moon, with rhythmic hopping steps, during the five-to-six-day Yaoshang festival (Manipur's spring festival coinciding with Holi) (Wikipedia, Dances of Manipur; Imphal Free Press). Traditionally performed in natural moonlight to folk songs accompanied by the pung drum and pena, it has long served as one of the few socially sanctioned occasions for young Meitei men and women to meet (Way2Barak; Imphal Free Press). Modern versions feature organised gatherings with bands playing drums, flutes and saxophones (Google Arts & Culture).
card.insight: Rooted in pre-Hindu Meitei society, the dance was elevated into a structured Yaoshang ritual after King Pamheiba adopted Gaudiya Vaishnavism around 1717, blending indigenous moonlight circle dances with Vaishnava devotion; it endures as a vehicle of community bonding and youth socialisation (Grokipedia; The Verandah Club).
